requestedActions.title: List file and folder names in the connected person's App Folder, continuing until all entries are listed

guide.summary: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 for user-authorized access. The requested read-only App Folder name listing maps to the files.metadata.read scope on list_folder and list_folder/continue, with continuation via the returned cursor. Each connected customer must authorize individually, and the app must be created with App Folder file access and registered redirect URIs. Distribution to other customer workspaces and any listing requirements remain unresolved.
guide.recommendation: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 for user-authorized access. findings.title: Use files.metadata.read for listing App Folder names
findings.detail: The documented required scope for list_folder and list_folder/continue is files.metadata.read, which covers reading metadata for listing entries. It does not grant file content download or write actions. Because the app uses App Folder access, the operations are limited to data within the app folder (/apps).
findings.appliesWhen: Customer OAuth token used to call list_folder and list_folder/continue for the App Folder.

findings.title: Select App Folder file access when creating the app

findings.title: Register the app key, secret and exact redirect URIs
findings.detail: Setup requires registering the app in the App Console to obtain an app key and secret (client_id and client_secret) and entering redirect URIs. Dropbox checks that the redirect_uri in the authorization URL matches a registered value. Customers should connect through the app's OAuth flow rather than registering their own Dropbox app.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first OAuth test because the client credentials and redirect configuration are needed to start authorization.

findings.title: Choose the OAuth flow by client type
findings.detail: Dropbox recommends the authorization code flow for server-side web apps with short-lived access tokens and no refresh tokens for interactive use. Client-side or unsecured-secret apps should use the code flow with PKCE (S256). The token is user-scoped and sent as a Bearer token.
findings.appliesWhen: Implementing customer authorization for the web app; PKCE applies if the client cannot keep a client_secret.

evidence.quote: is the recommended OAuth flow for all types of applications. In order to implement it, your application should:
A server-side web application that only calls the Dropbox API as users interact with it Use the OAuth code flow with short-lived access tokens only (no refresh tokens).
Public clients should use the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256).

findings.appliesWhen: Each customer organization or workspace user connects to the app during testing and use.

steps.title: List the first page of App Folder entries with list_folder
steps.detail: Boundary check: with a safe nonmutating call, POST /2/files/list_folder with path set to the empty string using the customer's OAuth token. Confirm the token carries files.metadata.read and that returned entries are inside the App Folder. If the boundary is unclear, inspect the actual grant and outgoing request log instead of assuming a narrower token grant. Read metadata only. No content download or writes. Retain the cursor and has_more from this first response. Pagination continues in later steps.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns HTTP 200 with entries, cursor and has_more. Names are read from entries, the cursor is retained, and the App Folder boundary and read-only scope are confirmed.

steps.title: Continue listing App Folder entries with list_folder/continue until has_more is false
steps.detail: Pagination: while has_more is true, POST /2/files/list_folder/continue with the cursor from the immediately previous list_folder or list_folder/continue response. Repeat with each new cursor and combine entries from every page. Stop only when has_more is false, as documented; do not treat two pages as a complete listing. Boundary check: reuse the same customer token and path root, keep the read-only files.metadata.read scope, and call no write endpoints.
steps.doneWhen: Each continuation returns HTTP 200 with entries and a new cursor, and the loop stops only when has_more is false, with all entries combined.

details.title: Choose the OAuth flow by client type
details.detail: Dropbox recommends the authorization code flow for server-side web apps with short-lived access tokens and no refresh tokens for interactive use. Client-side or unsecured-secret apps should use the code flow with PKCE (S256). The token is user-scoped and sent as a Bearer token.
details.appliesWhen: Implementing customer authorization for the web app; PKCE applies if the client cannot keep a client_secret.

preparation.title: Permissions rationale
preparation.text: files.metadata.read: The documented required scope for list_folder and list_folder/continue is files.metadata.read, with continuation via the returned cursor while has_more is true. App Folder file access limits the scope to /apps. This read-metadata scope does not provide content download or write actions.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register the Dropbox app with App Folder access and exact redirect URIs
In the App Console, create the app, select App Folder file access, enable files.metadata.read, register the exact redirect URI, and record the app key and secret. Dropbox checks the redirect_uri against the registered values.
Fields: app key from App Console (client_id), app secret from App Console (client_secret), exact redirect URI registered in App Console

Prepare the authorization code flow with PKCE code verifier and challenge
Prepare the web app code to build the Dropbox authorization URL with response_type=code and token_access_type=online, generate a PKCE code verifier and S256 challenge if the client cannot keep a secret, and handle the returned code and state. Do not execute consent in this step.
Fields: response_type=code, code_challenge_method=S256 when PKCE is used, state value for CSRF protection

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Have each customer account authorize the app individually on dropbox.com
Done when: The customer completes Dropbox consent and the app receives an authorization code or redirect for that individual account.

Exchange the authorization code for a user access token
Done when: The token response returns access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in and scope for the individual account.

List the first page of App Folder entries with list_folder
Done when: The response returns HTTP 200 with entries, cursor and has_more. Names are read from entries, the cursor is retained, and the App Folder boundary and read-only scope are confirmed.

Inspect the granted scope in the token response before listing
Done when: The developer records the scope string from the token response and confirms no write or content scope was requested.

Continue listing App Folder entries with list_folder/continue until has_more is false
Done when: Each continuation returns HTTP 200 with entries and a new cursor, and the loop stops only when has_more is false, with all entries combined.

Repeat list_folder/continue with the newest cursor until has_more is false
Done when: The final page returns has_more false, all entries from every page have been collected, and the App Folder boundary and read-only access are confirmed.
